flagged.comment: Building elevation drawings are not included in the bound plan set. The complete sheet index (39 sheets) contains no building elevation sheets; all architectural elevations are absent from the bound plan set. Elevations must be provided for all proposed buildings.

Building elevation drawings are not included in the bound plan set. All height information is presented only in tabular form on Sheet 9; architectural elevation sheets showing building facades, dimensions, and measurement methodology are required.

No building elevation drawings are included in the bound plan set (39 sheets). Building height information is provided only in tabular form on Sheet 9 (Building Height Table) and Sheet 29 (Finished Floor Elevations). Architectural elevation sheets must be included in the bound plan set and referenced in the Index of Sheets.

Elevation sheets are not provided for any of the eight buildings on the site, nor are elevations provided for any required sides of the buildings. Separate architectural elevation drawings must be provided for each building showing all required elevations (typically north, south, east, and west facades).

Elevation sheets are not provided for any of the eight buildings on the site. Elevation drawings must be provided for all buildings and for all required sides of each building to verify height measurement, AAG calculation, and roof type-specific measurement methodology.

Elevation sheets are not provided for any of the 8 buildings. No elevation views are shown for any sides of any building. Provide separate architectural elevation sheets for each of the 8 distinct building types, showing all visible elevations from cardinal directions.

For developments with multiple distinct building types, separate architectural elevation sheets are not provided for each building type. The site contains three distinct building types (4-Plex, 5-Plex, and 6-Plex); separate elevation sheets must be provided for each building type to demonstrate compliance with architectural standards.

The site includes three distinct building types (4-Plex, 5-Plex, and 6-Plex), but separate architectural elevation sheets are not provided for each type. Separate elevation sheets must be provided to document height, measurement methodology, and AAG calculation for each distinct building type.

The project includes multiple distinct building types (4-Plex, 5-Plex, and 6-Plex) as shown in the Building Data Table on Sheet 9, but no separate architectural elevation sheets are provided for each building type. Provide distinct elevation sheets for each building type.

Elevation sheets do not show the average adjacent grade (AAG) calculation identifying the highest and lowest grade points at the building perimeter, nor do they show the vertical dimension from AAG to the applicable measurement point. While Sheet 9 shows "Average (MSL)" values in the Building Height Table, no calculation is provided showing how the AAG was derived from highest and lowest adjacent grades at the building perimeter, and no vertical dimension line on elevation drawings connects AAG to the roof measurement point.

The Building Height Table on Sheet 9 shows 'Average (MSL)' values for each building, but does not explicitly show the AAG calculation formula (highest adjacent grade + lowest adjacent grade) ÷ 2, nor does it identify and label the highest and lowest grade points at each building perimeter. Elevation sheets must include the complete AAG calculation per LDC § 25-1-21(50).

Elevation sheets do not show the average adjacent grade (AAG) calculation. While the Building Height Table on Sheet 9 lists an 'Average (MSL)' value for each building (e.g., 686.25, 684.50, 685.00, etc.), it does not identify the highest and lowest grade points at the building perimeter or show the AAG calculation formula AAG = (highest + lowest) ÷ 2. The Grading Plan (Sheet 11) contains numerous spot elevations around buildings but lacks labeled AAG values and dimension lines from AAG to the roof point. Provide elevation sheets showing the highest and lowest grade points at each building perimeter (labeled 'AT BUILDING PERIMETER') and the vertical dimension from the calculated AAG to the applicable measurement point.

Height measurement method does not match roof type as required by LDC § 25-1-21(50). Without architectural elevation drawings showing the roof type and the applicable measurement point (coping for flat roofs, average height of highest gable for pitched/hip roofs, deck line for mansard roofs, highest point for other styles), the correct measurement method cannot be verified. Elevation sheets must clearly identify the roof type and show the measurement point used to comply with the code-required method.

The height measurement method cannot be verified from the site plan. No roof types (flat, pitched/hip, mansard, other) are designated on the site plan or in any drawings, and no measurement endpoints are specified. Elevation sheets must identify the roof type and show the applicable measurement point per LDC § 25-1-21(50): flat roof to top of coping; pitched/hip roof to average height of highest gable; mansard roof to deck line; other roof styles to highest point.

The Building Height Table on Sheet 9 does not specify the roof type for each building (flat, pitched, hip, mansard, or other), which is required to determine the correct height measurement methodology per LDC § 25-1-21(50). Different roof types require measurement to different points: flat roofs measure to the top of coping; pitched or hip roofs measure to the average height of the highest gable; mansard roofs measure to the deck line; other styles measure to the highest point. Provide elevation sheets identifying the roof type for each building and documenting that the correct measurement point was used for each roof type.

Building heights are shown in feet on the site plan data table (Sheet 9), but elevation sheets—which are the primary location for detailed height labeling—are not provided. Provide building elevation sheets with heights clearly labeled in feet from the average adjacent grade to the applicable roof point.

Building height is not labeled in number of stories on elevation sheets. While Sheet 9 notes 'Maximum Number of Building Stories = 3,' individual story counts are not labeled for each of the 8 buildings. Provide elevation sheets labeling the number of stories for each building.

Heights of individual buildings are shown in the Site Plan data table (Sheet 9) ranging from 33'-4.75" to 36'-1", with maximum height of 36'-1" (Building 3) identified, but no elevation sheets are provided where heights would be clearly separated by building. Provide architectural elevation sheets showing heights for each individual building.

Building height values show discrepancies across plan documents. The Building Height Table on Sheet 9 shows 'Average (MSL)' values (e.g., Building 1: 686.25, Building 2: 684.50) that differ from the Finished Floor Elevations shown on Sheet 11 Grading Plan and Sheet 29 Addressing Plan (e.g., Building 1: FFE 687.50, Building 2: FFE 685.50). The difference between 'Average (MSL)' and FFE is not explained, creating confusion about which value represents the grade baseline for height measurement. Ensure all height values are consistent across elevation sheets, site plan data tables, grading plan, addressing plan, and project narrative, and reconcile any differences with clear notation of whether values represent AAG, FFE, or finished grade at specific locations.

Compatibility height limit compliance cannot be verified. The site is subject to Article 10 compatibility standards per LDC § 25-2-1061 (MF-2 zoning within 75 feet of SF-3 triggering property). The applicable limits are: 40 feet maximum within 50 feet of triggering property; 60 feet maximum between 50–75 feet. However, the site plan does not show distance zone boundaries, does not identify the adjacent SF-3 property line, and does not document building locations relative to the triggering property. Distance zone notation and cross-sectional documentation are required to verify compliance.
areas: all eight buildings relative to SF-3 triggering property

flagged.comment: Compatibility distance zone boundaries are not shown on the site plan or elevation drawings. The site is subject to Article 10 compatibility standards per LDC § 25-2-1061. Elevation drawings must show the 50-foot and 75-foot distance zone boundary lines from the SF-3 triggering property and dashed reference lines at the applicable maximum permitted heights (40 feet within the 50-foot zone; 60 feet in the 50–75-foot zone) to graphically demonstrate compliance.
areas: all buildings relative to SF-3 triggering property

flagged.comment: Cross-sectional elevation views are not provided. A cross-section is required showing the building profile relative to the SF-3 triggering property line, with distance zone boundaries (50-foot and 75-foot) clearly labeled, proposed building heights in each zone, and maximum allowed heights for each zone, all drawn to scale with dimensions labeled. This graphical representation is necessary to verify compliance with Article 10 compatibility height limits per LDC § 25-2-1061.
areas: all buildings relative to SF-3 triggering property

flagged.comment: Rooftop structures above the maximum permitted building height are not labeled on elevation sheets as height limit exceptions. Without architectural elevation drawings, the presence of rooftop structures (parapets, mechanical equipment, chimneys, vents, stairways, elevator penthouses, etc.) and their relationship to the height limit line cannot be verified. Elevation sheets must clearly show and label any rooftop elements that extend above the maximum permitted building height.

Rooftop structure height exceptions cannot be verified without elevation sheets showing the height limit line and any overage calculations. The maximum allowable overage per § 25-2-531 is the greater of: (1) 15% of permitted height; (2) federal/state compliance amount; (3) engineering standard for stacks/vents; or (4) 30% for spires. Elevation sheets must provide a calculation demonstrating that any rooftop extensions remain within the allowable overage, with the calculation shown on the drawing.

For buildings subject to upper-story step-back requirements, the step-back location and dimensions are not shown on elevation sheets with required dimension callouts. The site plan does not document whether step-back requirements apply to these buildings. Elevation sheets must clearly show step-back locations, dimensions, and setback measurements if required by applicable zoning standards.
